<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge_source; a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource), metadataFields (literal, a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via isSystemObjectName (symbol, a top-level const), knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge_source; a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes), metadataFields (literal, a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4c6fcda00e5521fb61505af59d9858757983a16` — the merge of head `830150985dc08854ae7c5e59e7e2878b9a181a67` into base `bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4c6fcda00e5521fb61505af59d9858757983a16 && git checkout d4c6fcda00e5521fb61505af59d9858757983a16
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd 830150985dc08854ae7c5e59e7e2878b9a181a67 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd && git merge --no-ff 830150985dc08854ae7c5e59e7e2878b9a181a67

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfc0dd054ba4e05ba35cc3f77d8260c0e144f2bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f2c9aff7f75f2cc469ff19d3b20a1ddf63d946c9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-knowledge-source.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-knowledge-source.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-publish-refuses-missing-references-and-gated-objects.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: docs/adr/0161 (K4, K5, Execution), packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/core/src/utils/internal-write-response.ts, packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/ai-read-exposure.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts, packages/lint/src/system-fields.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-platform-global.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-package-addressing.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md and types.ts. The changeset and the four docs counts are read under ② and (e) because the order asks for it.

Inputs read: card #37307 body and its four comments (7165478297, 7216413780, 7219690738, 7219789648), PR #37971 body, file list (12 files) and net diff against main, PR comments (docs-drift 7219696503, review claim 7221551422), and the check-runs on the head. Every check-run on the head concluded success or skipped; none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

What the diff changes, each named right or wrong.

1. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint` grows by one function, five rule id constants and two types (index.ts). Right, and it is why `Clause-②: yes` holds.
2. Accept set at the runtime publish door narrows for `knowledge_source`: `runtime-gate.ts` maps the type to `knowledgeSources` and the registry entry is `tier: 'gating'`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['knowledge_source']`. The door runs the same function as the CLI, so the rule ids and message text are one set. Right as wiring. D1 still holds (a draft is not gated) and the differential charges only the written item.
3. Accept set of `os validate` / `build` / `lint` narrows: four error verdicts exit 1. Right in intent; wrong in two cases below (M1, S1).
4. `@objectstack/spec` gains one registered upgrade entry, no schema change. Right.

(a) The five findings, read against the platform's real rules.

The door's universe. `protocol-authoring-gate.ts` builds `objects` from `engine.registry.listItems('object')` (every registered object, every package, extensions folded) with the stored `sys_metadata` object rows and the batch's pending drafts folded in, then narrows it to the write's package closure when the write names a package (`narrowObjectsToWriteClosure`: the package, its declared dependencies, unpackaged overlay rows, and system objects unconditionally). The knowledge service resolves `source.object` through `engine.getSchema`, which is `registry.getObject`. So with no closure the door's universe contains everything the service can resolve: an object registered late in boot is present, because a runtime write happens after boot; a dependency's object is present; a tenant overlay object is present. Boot itself is not gated (the loader never calls lint), as the changeset says.

- `knowledge-source-object-unknown`.
  - Door, no closure: true. A name the registry does not carry is a name the index walk cannot read. One legacy corner: `registry.getObject` also folds a short name onto a legacy `NS__NAME` key, and lint matches the registered `name` exactly, so a source spelled by the short name of such a key is refused where the service resolves it. `object-graph.ts` already documents that stance for extensions (the refusing direction, remedy: write the registered key). Accepted as the package's standing rule.
  - Door, closure in force: an object of a package the manifest does not declare is refused although the host serves it and main's service would index it. This is the platform's standing closure rule (#9612; the flow trigger, list view and dataset doors give the same verdict), it is worded for the closure with the shared remedy, and the changeset declares it. Right.
  - Door, leniency: a known platform name that is absent, and a platform-prefixed name nothing registers, pass (skip, or warning) although the door holds the whole host universe. K4 says such an item is refused. See N3.
  - CLI: not the same verdict as the door. See S1.
- `knowledge-source-field-unknown`. True for a declared field, a field a stack extension adds, and every injected column with a definition. False for `id`. See M1.
- `knowledge-source-object-not-searchable`. It reads `canServeApiOperation(enable, 'search')`, the predicate and operation the admission module asks at gate 2, imported, not restated. That predicate reads three things: `enable.apiEnabled === false` refuses; a present `enable.apiMethods` list refuses unless it grants the `list` primitive; and `enable.searchable === false` refuses only when a list is present, because `apiExposureDenialReason` returns served for the unrestricted mode before any flag is read (api-derivation.ts:448-452). Does the runtime search refuse such an object? For every caller that is not the system identity, yes, through the same predicate (`admitSources`). For the system identity, no: `admitSources` and `admitAuthoredSource` return admitted on `ctx.isSystem`, and the index walk runs under a system context with no gate, so the source is indexed and a system-context search is served. See ④ for why that is still K4's own refusal, and N1 for the wording.
- `knowledge-source-system-object-not-ai-readable`. The same rule as admission gate 3: the `/^sys_/i` name test and `isAiReadExposed`. Admission also tests the schema's declared name; lint keys its map by that name, so the two agree. The stored-metadata family is refused whatever it declares, in both places.
- `knowledge-source-field-never-indexed` (warning). The same set as the service's withheld set. `recordToDocument` withholds `collectCredentialWriteResponseFields` plus `collectInternalWriteResponseFields`; the first is `isMaskedOnReadFieldType(def.type, schema.managedBy)` and the second is `def.internal === true`. The rule asks exactly those two, with the object's `managedBy`. A field with only a `maskingRule` is not in either set, in both places.

Could a refusal hit a source main serves correctly today? Yes, in two shapes: M1 (a member naming `id`) and S1 (a package whose source indexes a declared dependency's object, on the CLI). Not for inherited or extension fields, system columns other than `id`, late-registered objects, or dependency objects at the door.

(e) Transcript counts. `AUTHORING_RULES` holds 87 entries at this head and 86 on main (9a274e6725, which already contains #37870). The four transcripts read 87. True at this head. Main has not gained a rule since the merge base, so 87 is still right today; #37986 needs 88 if it lands second.

(h) Tests. The 37 cases pin each of the five ids through `runAuthoringRules('validate')` with severity, path and the named object or field; the door through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` with errors in `errors`, warnings in `advisories`, and the face equal to the CLI face; the dispatch and the stack key; the closure wording with a non-vacuous control; and passing controls (a clean source at both doors, `list` granting search, an `aiReadable` system object, injected columns, an extension field, an artifact sibling). Not pinned: a member naming `id` (M1), a source over a dependency's object on the CLI (S1), and `searchable: false` with no `apiMethods` list (N2). The 422 envelope at `saveMetaItem` is not asserted here; the generic gate tests own it.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right: new exports and a new refusal. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right: a requirement is tightened and a value that published is now refused. `@objectstack/lint` minor with the BREAKING banner follows the rule (a kind takes at least minor on a package the diff moves). `@objectstack/spec` patch for an entry-only change matches the sibling changesets on main (`35143-data-model-publish-checks`, `36595-related-list-key-under-arrangement`), and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Both declaration lines stand in the PR body and the changeset; one ADR-0087 marker, `registered`, names the entry id.

Upgrade entry. Shape: all four required `SemanticMigration` members, no `conversionIds` (right, no D2 conversion). File name `19.` plus the id, as the README derives it; major 19 is the current protocol major. Registration: the directory is the index and `registry.ts` is generated, so no second file is owed. Well formed. Its prescription text carries S1 and S2, and N1.

The changeset, sentence by sentence.
- Banner: "it was accepted before and is refused now (422 ...)". True for a missing object or field. For the two gates it is true only where no author judgement was reached (no knowledge service mounted, or a system-context write); a judged author already got 403 at save. The entry's `reason` says so; the banner does not. Acceptable.
- "`os validate` / `lint` / `compile` / `build` refuse the same source". True for the error verdicts, save S1.
- "The schema is unchanged, and stored sources are not rewritten or refused at boot." True.
- "Four errors, because a source that carries one indexes nothing". Not true as written. See N1.
- object bullet: true; the closure sentence is true.
- field bullet: "declared ... or injected by the platform (`owner_id`, `created_at`, …)". Omits `id`, which is M1.
- search bullet: "an `enable.apiMethods` list that grants neither `search` nor `list`, or `enable.searchable: false`". See S2 and N2.
- system bullet and warning bullet: true.
- "The two gates are the knowledge service's own search-time gates that need no caller, asked through the same spec predicates." True.
- FROM → TO line 1, "an object the stack or a declared dependency defines": does not clear the CLI error (S1). Line 2: right. Line 3, "an `apiMethods` list that grants `list` or `search`": S2. Line 4: right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (refuse at publish). The addendum reports a seat ruling, keep gating. No seat-signed ruling comment is among the inputs; the only text is the dev session's own attribution. Judged on K4 alone, the answer is the same: A, gating. See (c).
- Open question 2 (CLI severity of an unprefixed unknown object). Not answered anywhere in the thread. Answered here: S1.
- Open question 3 (declaration lines). A is right; see ②.
- (c) Ruling carry. Both quotations in the `Ruling-ref:` line match ADR-0161 on main character for character: the "Referencing objects" paragraph (line 169) and the "Source admission at save" bullet (line 174). The Execution table's "rows 4, 5, 5b" row carries "K4's reference checks and the gates that need no principal". `Premise corrected:` states the conflict fairly: the card's item 3 points at the advisory `ai_context` verdict while its item 4 and K4 say refused. K4 is the governing text, so the correction carries. One reading note: K4's "at publish" sentence speaks of a packaged item and the gates; the refusal of a missing object or field at the runtime door rests on "is refused when the object or a named field does not exist". That is a fair reading and it is the one the door needs.
- (f) Point 3, lint suite not re-run after the second main merge. The merge (73d5e347f7 to 0b539b6abb) brought two lint changes: `validateBookAudienceClaims` (#37870: one registry entry, `runtimeTypes: ['book']`, reads `stack.books`, plus its export and explain lines) and a lookup `dependsOn` check inside `validate-object-field-refs.ts` (#37910). Neither is dispatched on a `knowledge_source` write, neither reads `knowledgeSources`, and neither touches a helper this rule imports (`object-graph.ts`, `system-fields.ts`, `collection-entries.ts`). The new tests filter CLI findings by the `knowledge-source-` prefix, and the door admits only rules that declare the type. No interaction. Main since the merge base changed `packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` only. Test Core is green on the head, which is the gate verdict for the suite.
- (g) Point 4, the `object-api-not-served` text in `admitAuthoredSource`. The note is right and understates it. The text says the `enable.apiMethods` list "does not include `search`". `search` is a retired legacy value an author never declares (`LEGACY_API_METHODS`, object.zod.ts:102); it derives from `list` with `searchable` not false. So the text names a cause no author can act on, in every case and not only for `searchable: false`. Leaving `service-knowledge` untouched in this PR is right (the claim's fence). "Noted, not filed" is not: see N4. The PR repeats the same slip in its own prescriptions: S2.
- Deviations. The file surface grew past the claim by the upgrade entry and four docs counts; both are forced by gates (`check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`) and both are named in the PR body. Accepted. The three gate families not measured locally are answered by the head's check-runs.
- SQL push-down: the rule reads metadata only. No id materialisation, no join. Nothing to find.
- Security-touching: no, with the reason stated. The rule reads two exposure predicates and the credential-class declaration, so it is security-adjacent, but it moves no access decision: the search-time admission and the index's withheld set are unchanged and stay the enforcement, the rule only adds refusals, and nothing downstream relies on it. It cannot open a read. Its failures are false refusals and one leniency (N3), not exposure.
- Read-only shape: nothing was built, run or re-run. The head tree was read from a detached checkout of the head in the existing clone, restored to its prior commit afterwards.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself. K4 on main says a `knowledge_source` item "is refused when the object or a named field does not exist" and that the two principal-free gates are met "in `os validate` and at publish". The capability the gate takes away on main is real but narrow: a source over an `apiEnabled: false` object or a non-opted system object is indexed today and is served to a system-context search. K4 and its Consequences ("refused when it is written, not found empty when it is searched") order that refusal, so the PR makes the spec's own refusal real and does not narrow a declared capability at the consumer. The departure from the advisory `ai_context` row is right for the same reason and is stated at all three sites. Reusing the spec predicates and the admission module's readings, with no restated gate, is the right shape. The design holds; three points in its execution do not.

M1 (must-fix) — a source member naming `id` is refused as `knowledge-source-field-unknown`, at the publish door and on the CLI, although `id` exists on every object and main serves it. `fieldMapOf` builds the field set from the declared fields plus `injectedColumnDefsFor`, and that map leaves `id` out by contract: the primary key is the driver's, "no object document declares it and neither `/meta` exit serves it" (injected-system-column-provenance.ts). `system-fields.ts` says which helper to use: `injectedColumnsFor` "wherever the rule RESOLVES a field reference", and it does report `id`. The service's own reading admits `id` without a declaration (`freshnessFields`: `name !== 'id' && !names.has(name)`), and `recordToDocument` writes `record.id` into the hit's metadata when `metadataFields` names it. So `metadataFields: ['id']` is a valid, served source that this gating rule refuses with a false sentence ("the index reads nothing for it on any record"), and the upgrade entry's acceptance criterion would have the author delete a working member. K4 refuses a field that "does not exist"; this one exists. Fix: resolve existence through `injectedColumnsFor(def)` (a resolved name with no definition is addressable and of unknown type, so it takes no warning), add the pin, and name `id` in the explain entry and the changeset's field bullet. The same gap sits in `validate-ai-context.ts`, where it only advises: a follow-up card, not this PR.

S1 (should-fix) — on the CLI, an unprefixed object the stack and its artifact do not define is an error, and that refuses a package whose source indexes an object of a declared dependency the artifact does not carry. The door admits that same source: under the closure a declared dependency's object is in reach, and the door's own remedy is "Declare a dependency on the package that defines ...". An author who follows it then fails `os validate` and `os build`, because the CLI reads the stack's objects and `packages[]` only. The message is false there ("this stack does not define, so the source indexes nothing and no search ever returns a hit from it"), the hint names no fix that keeps the source, and the changeset's FROM → TO and the entry's `replacement` both promise that declaring the dependency resolves it. So the level is not consistent with the runtime door, and the PR's "one verdict at both doors" does not hold in this shape. "As in the validateObjectReferences ladder" is also only half true: that ladder skips an empty universe with no closure (`noUniverse`), skips an object the stack extends, and since #35143 advises where a build cannot see a dependency; this rule carries none of the three. The door can also be handed an empty `objects` when the registry read fails (`listRegisteredCollection` catches to `[]`), and then every source is refused with a sentence that blames the author. Error is the right level where the stack is enough to know: at the door, and on the CLI for a stack that declares no dependency it does not carry. Where the manifest declares one, the miss should be the `flow-trigger-unknown-object` split (warning with the hedge, error under a closure or against the whole collection), or the seat rules otherwise in the thread with the remedy text made true. Either way the open question needs its answer on the card, and the hint, the FROM → TO line and the entry must say what actually clears the finding.

S2 (should-fix) — the prescriptions tell a refused author to grant `search` in `enable.apiMethods`, and `search` is a retired value there. The authored enum is the six primitives; `search` is stripped at parse with a warning, ignored by `resolveEffectiveApiMethods`, and a list holding only it resolves to deny-all, which closes the object's whole API. The slip is in the rule message ("grants neither `search` nor `list`"), the rule header, the explain entry, the changeset's search bullet and FROM → TO line 3 ("grants `list` or `search`"), and the registered entry's `replacement` ("grants `search` or `list`"). The verdict is right; the stated fix is wrong in one arm, and the entry is published upgrade guidance. Fix: say the list does not grant `list`, and prescribe `list` with `searchable` not false, in all five places.

N1 (nit) — "a source that carries one indexes nothing" is the stated reason for the error level in the rule header, `KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_DOORS`, the changeset and the entry's `reason`, and it is true only of a missing object. A missing field leaves the rest of the document indexed (the field explain entry says so itself). A gated object is indexed, and a system-context search is served; what is true is that no caller the service judges is ever served a hit. K4 orders the refusal regardless, so the level stands; the sentence should say what happens.

N2 (nit) — `enable.searchable: false` is stated as a refusing cause without its condition. The predicate refuses on it only when an `apiMethods` list is present; `{ searchable: false }` alone is served for search, by this rule and by the admission. The rule is faithful to the predicate. Whether the unrestricted short-circuit in `apiExposureDenialReason` should read the flag is a spec question for its own card.

N3 (nit) — at the door with no closure, a platform-prefixed name nothing registers only warns and a known platform name that is absent is skipped, although the door holds the whole host universe and K4 says refused. Lenient, never a false refusal, and the same as the ladder it copies. A `wholeCollection` input, as `validateObjectReferences` takes, would close it: follow-up.

N4 (nit) — the `admitAuthoredSource` wording should be a filed card, not a note in a PR body, and its scope is the whole sentence (see (g)), so the fix there and S2 here use one wording.

N5 (nit) — the seat's "keep gating" ruling should stand in the thread as the seat's own comment; today only the dev session's attribution exists. The K4 text is enough for this record.

N6 (nit) — the entry has no `relevantWhen` (`stack-declares`, `knowledgeSources`), so every 18 to 19 upgrade lists it, with or without a knowledge source. The sibling knowledge-source entries omit it too; one follow-up for the family.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK** at head `f2c9aff7f75f2cc469ff19d3b20a1ddf63d946c9` (Fixes #37307). Full read · 2026-11-27T15:13Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** Check-runs at f2c9aff7: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. The two timeouts outside the diff passed on the one re-run. `!` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, so the contract tier is owed. Skills-docs now reads `#37310` (amendment 7221575164). The dogfood battery at 73441db425 was red only on 14 timeout files, which all passed when re-run alone. The main merge since then does not touch the publish-door mechanism, so I read the failures as box contention.
